title: Temsirolimus for kidney cancer

indication_text: First-line advanced renal cell carcinoma with at least three of six source prognostic risk factors
purpose: Help control advanced kidney cancer in the source-defined higher-risk setting.
schedule_summary: The usual dose is 25 mg by intravenous infusion over 30 minutes once a week. The NCCP calendar lists Days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of each 28-day cycle. Continue while helpful and tolerable; there is no routine week off.

agents.name: Temsirolimus
agents.mechanism: Temsirolimus inhibits a protein called mTOR, part of the signalling system that controls cell growth, protein production and blood-vessel development. This can slow tumour growth. mTOR also supports normal immune and metabolic functions, explaining infection risk and changes in glucose or cholesterol.
agents.explanation: Temsirolimus inhibits a protein called mTOR, part of the signalling system that controls cell growth, protein production and blood-vessel development. This can slow tumour growth. mTOR also supports normal immune and metabolic functions, explaining infection risk and changes in glucose or cholesterol.
risks: Reduced immunity and serious infection, including opportunistic infection or sepsis
Low blood counts: anaemia, infection and bruising or bleeding
Sore mouth, rash, nail changes, fatigue and swelling
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, appetite loss and taste changes
Raised glucose, cholesterol or triglycerides; electrolyte changes
Non-infectious lung inflammation (pneumonitis), sometimes serious or fatal
Infusion allergy, including severe reactions; facial or airway swelling (angioedema)
Kidney failure, impaired wound healing, bowel perforation and bleeding; increased risk of other cancers with immune suppression
agents.watch: Use gentle mouth care and report ulcers early. Review infection prevention, diabetes and lipid management. Preventive medicine against Pneumocystis pneumonia may be considered if you also take corticosteroids or other immune-suppressing medicines; it is not automatically required for everyone.

anatomy: Fever, shivers or feeling suddenly unwell can signal infection. Call promptly even without a high temperature.
Mouth ulcers, rash and nail changes can affect comfort and eating. Report soreness early and follow your care plan.
New cough or breathlessness may be infection or lung inflammation. Contact the team promptly; severe breathing difficulty is an emergency.
Glucose, cholesterol and liver tests can change. Report thirst, frequent urination, confusion or yellow skin/eyes.
Report vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake. Severe abdominal pain, black stools or vomiting blood needs urgent care.
Kidney injury and swelling can occur. Report reduced urine, rapid swelling or dehydration.
Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest tightness, dizziness, pain or swelling at the cannula.
Low cells may cause tiredness, bleeding or infection. Report unexplained bruises and wounds that do not heal.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: The pivotal poor-prognosis renal cancer trial compared temsirolimus with interferon alfa. Median overall survival was 10.9 versus 7.3 months. The current EMA table distinguishes the prespecified interim hazard ratio of 0.73 (95% confidence interval 0.58–0.92) from the final analysis of 0.78 (0.63–0.97). This historical comparison does not establish superiority over modern first-line combinations.

items.title: Fertility and contraception

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Discuss benefit, burden, alternatives including supportive care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment. Trial averages cannot predict your own outcome.
